Flamingos captain Harmony Chidi is planning a fresh outreach initiative to support people in need after Nigeria’s historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. The 17-year-old, who led Nigeria to a 2-1 victory over Japan in the final on November 7, said she intends to use part of the financial rewards promised to the team to bring smiles to people facing difficult circumstances. “I will be posting my plans for an outreach anytime soon,” Chidi told AIPS Media. The Bayelsa Queens striker has previously demonstrated her commitment to helping vulnerable people, visiting pregnant women and sick patients at a hospital in Owerri, Imo State, in July. “I’m this type that with the little I have, I make sure that someone smiles for me,” she added. President Bola Tinubu approved a five-year Federal Government Savings Bond worth ₦100m for each player, with the funds preserved until they turn 18. The head coach, Akeem Busari, was awarded N100m in cash, while members of the technical crew were allocated N50m each. The Senate also pledged N100m to the team, while Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu announced a reward of N10m for each player and member of the coaching crew, alongside iPhone 17 Pro Max devices and other gifts. Protests rock UniAbuja over FCTA land cuts LASG spends N120.8bn on ‘professional fees’ A’Ibom gov seeks 80,000 LG votes for Tinubu, APC Beyond her plans to give back, Chidi recently opened up about the family challenges she overcame before becoming captain of the world champions. She revealed that her mother initially opposed her football ambition and wanted her to get married following the early death of her father. Her grandmother, however, encouraged her to pursue the sport until her death. “When I started football, my mother didn’t want me to play. My father died early, so my mother wanted me to get married. It was my grandmother who stood by me and pushed me to play football. Unfortunately, my grandmother is late,” she told BBC Pidgin. The teenager also credited her foster father, Prince Chidi, owner of her grassroots team, Imo Strikers, with helping her sustain her ambition. “It wasn’t easy until I met my foster father, Prince Chidi. He is the owner of my grassroots team, Imo Strikers, and he encourages me, making sure that I achieve my dream,” she said. Chidi’s journey to the World Cup triumph was also threatened by a serious injury that ruled her out of the previous edition of the tournament. She had described the setback as the most difficult period of her career, revealing that she had considered an alternative plan after losing the support of some friends during her recovery. She eventually recovered to captain Nigeria to the title in Morocco, completing a remarkable comeback from a setback that once threatened to end her football dream.
